liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): A crazy guitar jam breaks out around the five-minute and ten-second mark [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-01-27.sbd.miller.97344.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 1 songs; 12 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Phil is higher in the mix, with snappy drumming and flamenco interplay; This tape is clearer and has less wear than the other recording [8][11]
- **gd68-01-27.sbd.jools.14736.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 1 songs; 13 min; rated 2.88/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is fine, though the jam itself is described as uninspired; The audio sounds a little choppy, and the feedback hurts the listening experience; The mix features the bass very high up and prominent in the recording [3][5][12]

## Around the show

- The reviewer questions if the Spanish Jam actually belongs to the listed date [3]
- A voice at the end says they will see the crowd next time in Seattle [4]
- Garcia faintly says, 'See you next time we're in Seattle,' confirming the date [9]
- This jam is the end of the show archived as January 23, 1968 [4]
- The reviewer finds no similarity between this jam and the one on the January 23 tape [6]
- Levels differ from other January and February shows, suggesting it is not mislabeled [8]
- This tape completes the Spanish Jam that was cut off on the January 23 recording [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-01-27.sbd.miller.97344.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [1]. Also: The band likely reused expensive eight-track reels, causing the tape flip between shows [14]
- **gd68-01-27.sbd.jools.14736.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Hollister; source: Soundboard [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1968-01-26 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1968-01-22-grateful-dead-poster/) [16]
